mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, which reduces discount rates for equity valuations and drives positive forward returns in the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when FEDFUNDS declines, as measured by a t-test p-value > 0.05 against a zero-return null hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% within a 3-month window signals weakening labor market conditions, which increases the likelihood of central bank rate cuts and triggers a flight to equity risk assets, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative or flat 20-day returns in 60% or more of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in private demand, which increases the probability of monetary policy accommodation and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative or insignificant coefficient (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 108.0 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real output, which increases the risk of stagflation and triggers a flight to quality, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 108.0, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains above 3.5%, the market prices in a prolonged monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the interaction term in a regression model is not negative and significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in residential construction (HOUST) above 1300.0 thousand units, combined with a concurrent rise in real personal consumption (RSAFS), signals a recovery in private demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in more than 60% of cases when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed thresholds, or the interaction term in a predictive model has a non-positive coefficient (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200k per month for two consecutive months signals strong labor market demand, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to a hawkish monetary policy stance and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 200k, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) on a year-over-year basis, combined with a falling industrial production (INDPRO), indicates a contraction in aggregate demand and real economic activity, which increases the likelihood of fiscal or monetary stimulus and triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in more than 60% of cases when both GDPC1 and INDPRO are in contraction, or the interaction term in a regression model is not positive and significant (p < 0.05).
